about: A known cost on every resource the ledger has a line for, one after the other: cpu time, a resident footprint touched page by page, bytes written to a file, and bytes exchanged over a loopback socket. The footprint is held to the end, so a poll of the resident size sees it.

not_exercised.net.tcp.retransmit: loopback does not retransmit, and a retransmission cannot be chosen without a lossy link, which needs privilege (netem)
not_exercised.gpu.mem: the lanes workload uses the device; a footprint on it is a later addition here
not_exercised.gpu.kernel: the lanes workload launches a known number of kernels
not_exercised.power.energy: the machine's energy, which no program sets to a known figure

trust.cpu_s: exact to a few microseconds on the main thread's cpu clock; the process's on-cpu time is that plus the interpreter's start, the page touching and the copies, a few hundred milliseconds at most
trust.memory: the footprint grows by `bytes` once every page is touched (one write per page); the resident size is the interpreter's own (about 10 MiB) plus that, so the peak is at least `bytes` above the first sample
trust.faults: touching `bytes` of fresh anonymous memory a page at a time is `bytes / page` minor faults, fewer when the kernel maps a transparent huge page at once (2 MiB per fault), so the count is between `bytes / 2 MiB` and `bytes / page` plus the interpreter's own few thousand
trust.file: exact at the system calls, on descriptor `fd`
